desc:
Browser extension maintenance and updates from Ecom Swift LLC begins with a fixed starter sprint: we review your live extension, fix compatibility problems, update old libraries and ship a first round of improvements.

## What does browser extension maintenance involve?

Browser extension maintenance is the regular work of keeping a published extension healthy as browsers, websites and store rules change. It includes reading console errors, fixing features that stopped working, updating libraries, trimming permissions and checking the listing against current policy.

An extension is never finished the way a printed document is. Chrome and Edge release changes on a steady schedule, and the sites your extension touches change on their own timetable. What worked last year can fail today without anyone touching your code.

## Why a live extension drifts out of shape

Drift is gradual. A library gets a security notice. A browser deprecates a call your code still uses. A website renames a button and your content script stops finding it. Users rarely write to tell you. They simply stop using the extension or leave a short, unhappy review.

A starter sprint stops the drift and shows you the real state of the project. You get a clear picture of what is fine, what was repaired and what to watch next. That picture makes later decisions cheaper, because you pay for known work instead of emergencies.

## What a maintenance sprint can cover

- A review of the code and the warnings shown on the browser's extensions page.
- Cleanup of console errors that appear during normal use.
- Fixes for features broken by browser or website changes.
- Updated libraries, checked so that nothing else breaks.
- A permission review, removing access the extension no longer uses.
- A check of startup time and memory use.
- A look at store policy notes that apply to your category.
- Tests in current Chrome and Edge on a clean profile.
- A short written health note summarizing what changed.
- A store-ready package and a plan for what comes next.

## How the sprint runs

We start by loading your extension, using every feature and noting what fails or warns. Then we sort the issues by risk: first anything that stops a feature or may trigger a store action, then speed and tidiness. We repair what fits the sprint, test in current browsers and package the update.

The three packages differ in how much we can fix. Basic handles the most urgent issues and clears console errors. Standard adds library updates, a permissions review, one small improvement and a written health note. Premium goes deeper into startup and memory use, includes two improvements, checks the current store rules and finishes with an upkeep plan and a period of follow-up fixes.

If you want ongoing monthly care afterward, we quote that separately based on what the sprint shows.

## Do and avoid with a live extension

**Do:**
- Keep a list of the sites and features that matter most.
- Release small updates often rather than rare large ones.
- Read the store's developer emails as soon as they arrive.
- Test after each browser release channel update.
- Keep the source code in a repository with history.

**Avoid:**
- Ignoring a warning because the extension still loads.
- Updating every library at once without testing.
- Shipping a fix directly to all users with no check.
- Leaving permissions in place that no feature uses.
- Waiting for users to report problems before looking.

## Who this is for

It suits an owner of an extension that has not been touched for a long time. It suits a business whose extension began to misbehave after a browser update. And it suits a founder who wants a baseline before deciding whether to invest in a larger redesign.

## What we need from you

Send the source code or a repository invite, the store link and a list of things you already know are wrong. Mention the browsers your users prefer and any feature you most want improved.

We never ask for passwords. If you want the update published, we describe the steps clearly or you can add us to the store dashboard at the access level it offers. After you order, we send a short checklist and begin with the review.
